data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** $(git rev-parse HEAD)

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

When a test uses grep/awk/sed against a target artifact that has no behavioral surface (workflow YAML, skill markdown, agent prompt, contract markdown, dso-config.conf, .github/instructions/*), source-grep is the correct testing approach. The artifact under test IS structural documentation — there is no runtime to execute. The reviewer should NOT cite Behavioral Testing Standard Rule 3 ("Execute, don't inspect") against these tests because Rule 3 was written for code under test, not contract documents.

#### Actual Behavior

The test-quality reviewer (and standard reviewer when reviewing test files) reflexively cites Rule 3 against any test that greps a structural artifact. Observed on PR #197 with 3 critical/important findings against legitimate workflow-YAML structural assertions. The team was forced to add a narrow exception to reviewer-delta-standard.md (PR #199, bug da45-7d92-6c86-42bc) covering only the REMOVAL case ("removing source-grep tests is intended cleanup"). The PRESENCE case — keeping a source-grep test that asserts on the structure of a workflow file or skill — is still flagged as Rule 3 violation.

#### Evidence

* PR #197 cycle findings (3 of 7 review findings):
  - test_test_hooks_job_exists flagged critical [Source-file-grepping] for grepping workflow YAML
  - test_review_needs_test_hooks_and_test_scripts flagged critical for parsing workflow with awk
  - PR #188 test-ci-llm-review-job.sh:328 flagged critical for inspecting workflow YAML rather than executing
* Recurrent: DEFENSE_RECORD migrated from PR #194 — "grepping plugins/dso/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md for structural contract anchors" (owning ticket 3818-310d) — re-fires across multiple PRs touching onboarding structural tests.
* PR analysis (15 most recent merged PRs, 27 DSO findings total): source-grep mis-flag is the dominant FP class — 7 findings = 26% of total = 44% of FPs.

### 3. Action History

* PR #199 added a NARROW exception to reviewer-delta-standard.md covering the REMOVAL case only.
* The PRESENCE case remains uncovered.

### 4. Proposed Fix

Add a typed structural-test exception to reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (and cross-reference in reviewer-delta-standard.md): when the test's target artifact is in {workflow YAML files under .github/workflows/, skill markdown under plugins/dso/skills/**/SKILL.md and related .md, agent prompt markdown under plugins/dso/agents/*.md, contract markdown under plugins/dso/docs/contracts/*.md, dso-config.conf, .github/instructions/*}, source-grep IS the correct approach — Rule 3 does not apply. Require the reviewer to identify target-artifact type before emitting a Rule-3 / [Source-file-grepping] / [Tautological] finding against structural assertions.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* Affected agents: code-reviewer-test-quality, code-reviewer-standard
* Affected deltas: reviewer-delta-test-quality.md, reviewer-delta-standard.md
* Affected build: build-review-agents.sh
* Research support: docs/findings/code-review-fp-research-2026-05-17.md §9 (proposal A)

### 6. Logs

Estimated effect of fix: kills 80–90% of source-grep mis-flags → –21–23% on FP rate (from 59% → ~36-38%).
data.title: [code-reviewer-test-quality]: source-grep tests on structural artifacts -> Rule-3 over-application false positives
